task: Fix the incorrect rate limit enforcement after the API key scope validation was bypassed.

candidate_memories.content: API keys with the read-only scope are successfully submitting write requests after the scope validation was removed.
The scope validation middleware must be re-enabled; it was disabled to fix an unrelated authentication bug.
The middleware was temporarily disabled two weeks ago and the re-enable step was never completed.
All API key types are affected; both read-only and admin keys can now submit write requests.
Session 6 note: the security team requested a post-incident report after discovering the scope validation bypass.
API keys have three scopes: read-only, read-write, and admin.
Session 5 note: the security team completed an API key audit and found no scope violations before the disable.
Old practice: scope validation was done per-route before middleware-based validation was introduced.
The API key validation middleware runs before the authentication middleware in the chain.
Session 10 note: the auth team added rate limiting per API key scope.
Old middleware guide: scope validation was added in version 3.2 after the initial read-only scope was introduced.
When disabling middleware for debugging, create a follow-up ticket to re-enable it before the session ends.
Session 7 note: the security team requested a middleware audit log for scope validation events.
API key scopes are enforced at the middleware level; route handlers do not re-check scope.
Session 3 note: a penetration test found no scope bypass vulnerabilities before the middleware was disabled.
The API gateway additionally enforces method-level restrictions based on the API key scope.
Middleware disables for debugging must be time-bounded with an automated re-enable to prevent security regressions.
Session 12 note: the compliance team requested scope enforcement logs for their quarterly audit.
Old API key guide: the original API key design had no scope concept; scopes were added after the first security audit.
API key creation requires admin privileges and logs the key metadata but not the key value.
